claims.text: RWY work integrally in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) and prove that \(J_v\) is generated by two Schur-interval families; their proof uses Pieri identities and induction, not a stated Smith-form or unimodular-minor theorem. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 828-892]

833: Thus H^{\star}(G/P_{J},{\mathbb{Z}}) has {\mathbb{Z}}-basis given by
834: \{\sigma_{w}:w\in W^{J}\}=\{s_{\lambda}:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^{r}\}.
835: 4.4. A shorter presentation in type A
836: Starting with Theorem 2.3 , our goal is to find
837: an even smaller set of generators for the ideal J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}
838: within the coinvariant algebra, so that through ( 1.6 )
839: we obtain an even shorter presentation of I_{w} in type A.
840: First note that even though our proof of Theorem 2.3
841: for all finite Coxeter groups was done
842: in \Bbbk[V]/(\Bbbk[V]^{W}_{+}) where the field \Bbbk has characteristic zero,
843: the same proof works in type A more generally for the integral
844: coinvariant algebra H^{\star}(G/B,{\mathbb{Z}}). This follows since
845: the Schubert polynomials \{\mathfrak{S}_{w}\} satisfy the integer
846: coefficient versions of all of the requisite properties (a)-(g) used in Section 2 .
847: The bigrassmannian v_{r,s,t,n} described explicitly in ( 4.3 )
848: is r-grassmannian, and corresponds to the j\times i
849: rectangular partition i^{j}, where we define
850: \displaystyle i
851: \displaystyle:=s-t+1,
852: \displaystyle j
853: \displaystyle:=r-t+1.
854: When u and v are r-grassmannian and correspond respectively to
855: partitions \lambda and \mu, the Bruhat order relation u\geq v
856: is equivalent to inclusion \lambda\supseteq\mu of their Young
857: diagrams, meaning that \lambda_{i}\geq\mu_{i} for all i. Thus
858: Theorem 2.3 says that J_{v_{r,s,t,n}} is
859: generated as an ideal of \Lambda/I_{r,n-r} by
860: (4.4)
861: \{\mathfrak{S}_{u}:\mathrm{Des}(u)=\{(r,r+1)\},\,\,u\geq v_{r,s,t,n}\}=\{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^{r}\}.
862: This presentation from Theorem 2.3 can be
863: improved in type A_{n-1} as follows:
864: Theorem 4.8 .
865: Given a bigrassmannian v=v_{r,s,t,n} in type A_{n-1} with \mathfrak{S}_{v}=s_{i^{j}}, let
866: \displaystyle a
867: \displaystyle:=\min(n-r-i,r-j)
868: \displaystyle b
869: \displaystyle:=\min(i,j).
870: Then J_{v} is generated as an ideal of
871: H^{\star}(G/P_{J},{\mathbb{Z}})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r} by
872: (4.5)
873: \{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^{b},i^{j-b})\}.
874: Alternatively, J_{v} is generated by
875: (4.6)
876: \{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^{j},b^{a})\}.
877: We delay our proof of Theorem 4.8 until Section 4.7 .
878: Note that in both of the asserted generating sets ( 4.5 ) and ( 4.6 ) for J_{v},
879: the shapes \mu indexing the generators s_{\mu} run through an interval between
880: the j\times i rectangular shape i^{j} and the disjoint union of i^{j} with a
881: smaller rectangle of shape a\times b or b\times a.
882: In ( 4.5 ) the smaller rectangle is to the right
883: of the rectangle i^{j}, with both top-justified, while in ( 4.6 ) the
884: smaller rectangle is below the rectangle i^{j}, with both left-justified.
885: Thus in both cases, the generating sets have size \binom{a+b}{a}
886: and consist of generators whose multiset of degrees
887: have generating function
888: \sum_{\mu}q^{|\mu|}=q^{ij}\left[\begin{matrix}a+b\\
889: a\end{matrix}\right]_{q},
890: where \left[\begin{matrix}a+b\\
891: a\end{matrix}\right]_{q} is a q- binomial coefficient or Gaussian polynomial
892: [ M91 , I.2 Exer. 3] .

claims.text: The stated St. Dizier–Yong algorithm is a terminating tensor reduction for valid \((n,r,i,j,a,b,N)\), not a theorem about integer Pieri presentation matrices, determinantal divisors, Smith diagonals, or complementary minors. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 494-516]
